objective.statement: Cut API p95 latency in src/api/ in half, measured with the existing k6 script in perf/, without adding caching, changing the public response schema, or adding new dependencies.
objective.success_definition: The p95 latency of the API code in src/api/, as measured by the existing k6 script in perf/, is reduced to at most 50% of the pre-change baseline.

goals.statement: Reduce API p95 latency for code in src/api/ to at most half of its current baseline.
acceptance: Running the existing k6 script in perf/ after the change reports a p95 latency value that is ≤ 50% of the baseline measured by the same script before the change.

constraints.statement: Do not change the public response schema.
Latency must be measured with the existing k6 script in perf/.

assumptions.statement: The existing k6 script in perf/ is functional and produces a p95 latency measurement usable as a before/after comparison baseline.
The 50% latency-reduction target applies to the aggregate p95 measured by the k6 script, rather than requiring every endpoint under src/api/ to individually halve its p95.

open_questions.question: Does the 'cut p95 in half' target apply to aggregate p95 across the API surface in src/api/, or must each endpoint in src/api/ individually halve its p95?
options: Aggregate p95 across src/api/ as reported by the k6 script
Per-endpoint p95 for every route under src/api/

verification.spec: Run the existing k6 script in perf/ against the code before the change to capture baseline p95, then run the same script after the change and compare reported p95 values.
verification.expected: Post-change p95 is ≤ 50% of the pre-change baseline p95 reported by the same k6 script.

deliverables.description: Performance optimization changes within src/api/ that reduce API p95 latency by at least half.

factors: Hard constraints (no caching, no schema change, no new dependencies) significantly narrow the available optimization techniques.
Latency work in request-handling code carries regression risk for API behavior.
Baseline measurement quality depends on the existing k6 script in perf/.
